conclusion: No measured vision quality or efficiency advantage. All three generated candidates are byte-identical and mask route b. Topology A passes, topology B fails even after the transport recovery.
scenario: Real pinned Apache Flink code with two synthetic raw-job-name log calls and a shared verified sanitizer. Synthetic diagrams swap internal/external recipients; no claim about an actual Flink deployment vulnerability.

quality.initialVisionB: ReadTimeout before any final output; no patch generated

timingSeconds.note: Measured request durations, not full workflow wall time; unloading/idle time excluded. Includes cold model load. Single sample, not stable latency estimate.

observations: CSI configured static scan reported zero findings on the mutated source.
Code-only model acknowledged UNKNOWN deployment binding but guessed route b; it coincidentally matches topology A.
Vision A explicitly paired each route with its recipient and produced a correct patch, identical to the code-only patch.
Vision B listed correct logger/collector names, but listed recipients separately without explicit route-recipient pairs. The coder reported missing binding and still guessed route b.
Topology B leaves phone numbers in the actual external route a and masks the authorized internal route b: three security tests and one internal functionality test fail.
All helper checks and Java compilation pass. Earlier v2 regex compilation failure was removed by giving both arms the same tested helper, not by vision.
nextChange: Require explicit per-route logger -> recipient -> authorization -> source-call handoff records and block ungrounded edits. Validate instruction binding before the coder; do not silently supply evaluator ground truth.
limits: Synthetic injected diagnostic calls on real Flink. Collector ownership is deliberately outside source and supplied by diagrams.
Both conditions receive a working sanitizer: evaluates where to apply protection, not ability to invent sanitization code.
Code-only input is identical across deployments. One generated candidate is evaluated under both bindings; not two independent inference trials.
Two fresh image calls and two fresh vision-informed coder calls, one per deployment. No candidate repair or discarded model results.
Missing-fact abstention is legitimate; lower patch coverage does not imply worse uncertainty calibration.
No text control; added deployment information is measured, not image-exclusive capability.
Targeted tests capture logger outputs; no real external collector, full-cluster or repository navigation test.
Earlier no-patch/compilation/security failures are retained in deployment-boundary and deployment-boundary-handoff-v2.
